speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, as well as episodes of pain with urination. You also mentioned a history of a painful, swollen left ankle joint that resolved without treatment. Can you tell me more about these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any discharge from your penis or any eye redness and pain? I would also like to examine your knee and look for any skin rashes. REQUEST TEST: Urine_NAAT

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your sexual history and symptoms, the negative urine test makes gonorrhea or chlamydia less likely as the primary cause, though not impossible. Do you have any current eye redness, pain, or visual changes, and have you noticed any skin rashes, particularly on your palms or soles?

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any redness, pain, or discharge in your eyes, or any unusual skin rashes on your palms or soles? I need to rule out the ocular and dermatological manifestations often associated with reactive arthritis.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you have denied eye and skin symptoms, I need to confirm if the joint pain migrates, as your history of a resolving left ankle followed by right knee involvement suggests asymmetric oligoarthritis. Does the pain in your joints shift from one location to another, or have you noticed any lower back pain or stiffness in the morning?

speaker: Doctor
text: Your clinical presentation of asymmetric oligoarthritis, urethritis, and high-risk sexual history is highly suggestive of reactive arthritis, even with a negative initial urine NAAT. I will request further imaging and serological tests to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes. REQUEST TEST: HLA-B27, ESR, CRP, Rheumatoid_Factor, Anti-CCP REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal inflammatory markers and negative serology make systemic autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis unlikely, but do not rule out reactive arthritis. Given your specific history of urethritis followed by asymmetric joint swelling, I am proceeding with a clinical diagnosis of reactive arthritis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis
